functionalObligations.text: a route across several venues on one chain is constructed for a caller who named no venue; the caller may only supply an include or exclude list of DEXs and receives back a routePlans array of paths and per-DEX allocations
the route is computed off-chain on the operator's own servers and handed to the caller as pre-built calldata; no route search, quote or comparison of alternatives occurs on-chain and none is recorded
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Ag reads as an on-chain route-construction mechanism. Here the mechanism is a private server and a latency figure: the router contract executes a decision it did not make and cannot check. Nothing in the 58 distinguishes 'the protocol computes a route' from 'a vendor computes a route and the chain executes it'. There is no repository and the BSC implementation is unverified, so the substance is unfalsifiable from outside.

functionalObligations.text: the party that authored the route neither settles the trade nor bears price risk: the user signs and broadcasts an ordinary chain-native transaction and any adverse move between quote and inclusion is the user's
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a deliberate null. In, Rf and Ba each presume a counterparty distinct from the signer; none is present. This absence is a fact about LiquidMesh rather than a failure of the vocabulary, and it is recorded so stage 3 does not read the thin decomposition as a gap in the tables.

functionalObligations.text: settlement reverts unless the amount received meets a minimum return fixed in the signed calldata
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. In is the nearest and is rejected: L12 requires signed constraints plus a settlement verifier plus a solver or fallback plus a timeout, and here the signer is the executor, so two of the four parts are vacuous. No element names a settlement-enforced output floor on a self-executed swap. This obligation recurs in all five applications of this category and is the single most common residue in it.

functionalObligations.text: a quote is refused outright when the computed price impact exceeds the operator's threshold, returning error 40106 rather than a worse price
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. A pre-trade refusal to serve on an execution-quality ground. Aw gates identity, not the quality of the trade being requested.

functionalObligations.text: the signed transaction may be handed back to the operator for broadcast through private channels rather than the public mempool, at one of two privacy grades on EVM (public, private) or three on Solana (off, reduced, secure)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No element in the 58 names a transaction's path to inclusion, and none names a graded privacy level over that path. This is one of the two things LiquidMesh actually sells.

functionalObligations.text: the builders and validators that receive the flow are forbidden by agreement from auctioning the user's transaction, and the flow is not disclosed to third-party searchers
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Order-flow ownership expressed as a negative covenant rather than as a sale. The operator holds a right over the flow it constructs and exercises it by forbidding downstream resale. The vocabulary has four symbols for how an order is matched and none for who holds it or what they may do with it.

functionalObligations.text: the operator extracts MEV by backrunning the very transactions it built, and returns the majority of the proceeds to the trader; on Solana it instead buys priority through staked-validator and Jito paths and returns a portion of the saved tips
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Simultaneously extraction and protection, by the same party, on the same order. No element names either half. No percentage or formula is published, so the size of the rebate is UNKNOWN.

functionalObligations.text: the guarantee sold is inclusion rather than price: quote latency, quote freshness for newly created tokens, landing rate and uptime are the published product properties
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Every symbol in the 58 presumes inclusion and therefore cannot express reliability of inclusion as the thing being bought.

functionalObligations.text: a commission in basis points, taken from either the input or the output token at the caller's election, is charged on the trade and paid to the integrating wallet; the protocol defines the lever and collects nothing itself
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Fd is the nearest and is rejected: Fd names distribution of a protocol's own surplus or fees, whereas this is a fee the protocol defines, does not collect and does not distribute, so that whoever owns the user may tax them. Selling the monetization right rather than exercising it has no symbol. The mechanism is a named API parameter, not an abstraction.

functionalObligations.text: the only benchmark offered against the returned route is the operator's own midPrice and priceImpactPct in the same response; no external reference price, no price-improvement measurement and no record of the alternatives considered is published
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Price-improvement benchmarking, stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. The benchmark and the thing benchmarked are produced by the same party in the same response. X14 concerns an exclusive market structure plus a price-improvement claim with no named benchmark; the second limb holds here, the first does not, because LiquidMesh owns no venue.

functionalObligations.text: no party other than the user may fill a LiquidMesh order: there is no solver set, no auction, no RFQ tier, no maker and no filler of any kind
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, recorded as a null. Solver eligibility, stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. The vocabulary can no more say 'this system has no filler market' than it can say what a filler market's entry rule is; the absence is invisible to a decomposition, which is why LiquidMesh and KyberSwap collide on Ag.

functionalObligations.text: a request originating from a listed restricted territory, or detected as VPN or proxy masked, is refused a quote with error 42106
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. Aw is an on-chain permission gate over a protocol; this gate is off-chain, applied by the operator at the quote endpoint, and is not enforced by the router contract, which anyone may call directly. Standing principle used throughout this lane: Aw is used where a gate decides who may obtain the service, and is NOT used where a gate decides who may fill someone else's order (see F12, and KyberSwap F10).

functionalObligations.text: trades touching tokenized US equities (bStock) are refused to a second and much longer list of 57 further jurisdictions under its own error code 42107
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. Aw carries the refusal but cannot condition it on the instrument class being traded. Securities-style per-instrument geo-gating inside a swap-routing API is residue in everything but the bare refusal.

functionalObligations.text: the end-user address supplied with the request is screened against hack-associated and high-risk address lists before a quote is issued; supplying it became mandatory after a security update
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. Aw gates a holder's permission; this screens a counterparty's transaction history against third-party vendor lists. Same direction, different object.

functionalObligations.text: the token being traded is itself screened for scam and honeypot characteristics before a quote is issued
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. An asset-quality gate. Aw gates parties, not assets, and no other symbol names a protocol-assigned risk classification of the traded token as a precondition of service. Jupiter F16 is the same gap in a different form.

functionalObligations.text: the user grants token allowance to a standing approval contract that is separate from the router, so the allowance outlives the trade it was granted for
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. Au is a delegated execution scope and L17 requires bounded scope, revocation, expiry and nonce or domain separation; an ERC-20 allowance to a router-owned approval contract has revocation only. Arms X16 (unbounded delegated authority or unlimited token approvals).

functionalObligations.text: the router deployed on BSC is an upgradeable proxy whose implementation the admin may replace, and the implementation it currently points at is not verified
functionalObligations.note: Verified as an OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy, solc 0.8.17, EIP-1967, implementation 0x16F8a2735160E6c4614343959f82a9E1512BD14B which is NOT verified. L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is not discharged: no timelock, guardian or admin identity is published. X9 (Up with immediate single-key control) cannot be cleared because the admin is UNKNOWN. Departure from the corpus, which decomposed LiquidMesh to {Ag} alone.

functionalObligations.text: a bonding-curve launchpad is a first-class venue class, with dedicated trade types in the quote API and its own token-manager contract on BSC
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE by construction of the vocabulary: Bc (bonding-curve issuance) sits in the contested register and is therefore outside the 58. The router transacts against a bonding curve as an ordinary venue and the decomposition cannot say so.

functionalObligations.text: the same service is offered across EVM chains, Solana, Sui and Tron as independent per-chain routers; no value crosses a domain and no message is verified between domains
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a deliberate negative for stage 3: Xf and Xm are NOT discharged. Multi-chain presence is not a cross-chain mechanism, and the vocabulary has no way to state chain breadth as a competitive property. 96.9 percent of volume is on one chain (BNB Chain).

paper.title: LiquidMesh
paper.label: cat:int:liquidmesh
paper.blurb: A router with no public repository and no identified operating entity, whose implementation contract is unverified on the explorer for the chain it works on. It reaches the corpus on volume alone. The element-set decomposition records it as decomposing to a single element, and on the mechanism of routing that is correct.
paper.witnessReason: The witness adds a delegated-execution scope and a permission gate on evidence of the settlement path, and keeps the routing element the element-set decomposition assigns. It adds nothing for the venue's economics, because nothing in the vocabulary answers to them.
paper.residueNote: The element-set decomposition records this venue and one other as having identical decompositions. They do --- and their residue is disjoint. This one sells latency and takes the other side of the flow it routes; the other owns pools where it is the only permitted taker. Two systems can agree on every symbol the vocabulary has and share no economic mechanism at all, which is a sharper statement of non-identifiability than a collision on its own.
